strings.d1.s0.name: Phuket Old Town Thalang Road
strings.d1.s0.tips: Colourful Sino-Portuguese shophouses. Cafes open in the morning, and on Sundays the street turns into a walking market.
strings.d1.s1.name: Phuket Thai Hua Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: The history of Chinese migrants, in an air-conditioned old school building.
strings.d1.s2.name: One Chun Cafe Phuket
strings.d1.s2.tips: Michelin Bib Gourmand local cooking. Try the moo hong (braised pork belly) and the crab.
strings.d1.s3.name: Big Buddha Phuket
strings.d1.s3.tips: A 45 m marble Buddha on the hilltop with 360° views of the island. Cover shoulders and knees; get there by taxi or scooter.
strings.d1.s4.name: Wat Chalong
strings.d1.s4.tips: Phuket's most important temple, known for its tradition of making wishes with fireworks.
strings.d1.b0.name: Kopitiam by Wilai
strings.d1.b1.name: Khao Rang Hill
strings.d1.b1.tips: A hilltop with city views, close to Big Buddha. A good alternative.
strings.d2.s0.name: Kata Noi Beach
strings.d2.s0.tips: A small, calm cove. Sunbeds cost 100 THB, and in the dry season you can snorkel.
strings.d2.s1.name: Kata Beach Street Stalls
strings.d2.s1.tips: Pad thai and mango sticky rice just behind the beach.
strings.d2.s2.name: Karon Beach
strings.d2.s2.tips: 3 km of sand. The wind picks up in the afternoon; good for a long walk.
strings.d2.s3.name: Karon Viewpoint
strings.d2.s3.tips: A lookout that takes in three bays at once. Go before sunset.
strings.d2.s4.name: Kata Night Market
strings.d2.s4.tips: A night market in central Kata with grilled seafood and roti.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kampong Kata Hill Restaurant
strings.d2.b0.tips: A Thai restaurant full of antiques, in Kata.
strings.d2.b1.name: Dino Park Mini Golf
strings.d2.b1.tips: A rainy-day option for families with kids, in Karon.
strings.d3.s0.name: Maya Bay
strings.d3.s0.tips: Speedboat tour (~1,800 THB, lunch included, hotel pickup at 08:00). Visits to Maya Bay are limited; you also stop at Pileh Lagoon and Viking Cave.
strings.d3.s1.name: Pileh Lagoon
strings.d3.s2.name: Phi Phi Don Tonsai Village
strings.d3.s2.tips: Lunch in the island village (included in the tour) and a stroll through the shops.
strings.d3.s3.name: Bamboo Island
strings.d3.s3.tips: White sand and a last swim. The return leaves at 17:00.
strings.d3.s4.name: Rawai Seafood Market
strings.d3.s4.tips: Pick your fish at the market in Rawai and have it cooked across the way. Phuket's most famous seafood evening.
strings.d3.b0.name: Kan Eang at Pier Chalong
strings.d3.b0.tips: Seafood at Chalong Pier, as an alternative to Rawai.
strings.d3.b1.name: Coral Island Koh Hae
strings.d3.b1.tips: A nearby island for a half-day trip if Phi Phi is cancelled.
strings.d4.s0.name: Freedom Beach
strings.d4.s0.tips: An unspoilt cove reached by long-tail boat from Patong (~200 THB per person). The water is clear in the dry season.
strings.d4.s1.name: Patong Beach
strings.d4.s1.tips: The island's busiest beach. Good for walking and jet skiing (haggle).
strings.d4.s2.name: No.6 Restaurant Patong
strings.d4.s2.tips: A cheap Thai eatery in Patong. The queue moves fast; order the tom yum.
strings.d4.s3.name: Jungceylon Shopping Mall
strings.d4.s3.tips: An air-conditioned mall, handy for a break from rain or heat.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bangla Road
strings.d4.s4.tips: Patong's nightlife street, with bars and shows. Watch your wallet.
strings.d4.b0.name: Baan Rim Pa Patong
strings.d4.b0.tips: Royal Thai cuisine on the cliffs. Come for the sunset.
strings.d4.b1.name: Simon Cabaret Phuket
strings.d4.b1.tips: A cabaret show, as an alternative to Bangla Road.
strings.d5.s0.name: Nai Harn Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: The island's best-loved quiet beach, with a lagoon and pine shade.
strings.d5.s1.name: Nai Harn Beach Stalls
strings.d5.s1.tips: Grilled food and fruit shakes just behind the beach.
strings.d5.s2.name: Windmill Viewpoint
strings.d5.s2.tips: A viewpoint by the wind turbine, looking over Nai Harn and Ya Nui.
strings.d5.s3.name: Promthep Cape
strings.d5.s3.tips: The island's southernmost tip and Phuket's most famous sunset. Arrive an hour early to get a spot.
strings.d5.b0.name: Rawai Beach Restaurant
strings.d5.b0.tips: Thai food on the Rawai seafront.
strings.d5.b1.name: Ya Nui Beach
strings.d5.b1.tips: A tiny snorkelling cove below Promthep.
strings.d6.s0.name: Similan Islands
strings.d6.s0.tips: Open from November to May. Thailand's best islands for snorkelling and diving, reached by speedboat (~3,500 THB), with hotel pickup at 06:00.
strings.d6.s1.name: Similan Boat Lunch
strings.d6.s1.tips: Lunch is included in the tour.
strings.d6.s2.name: Sailing Rock Koh Miang
strings.d6.s2.tips: The Similans' signature rock, with views from the top.
strings.d6.b0.name: Khao Lak Seafront Restaurant
strings.d6.b1.name: Racha Island
strings.d7.s0.name: Old Town Soi Romanee
strings.d7.s0.tips: The most photogenic street, best in the morning light.
strings.d7.s1.name: Torry's Ice Cream Phuket
strings.d7.s1.tips: Local ice cream in Old Town. Go for coconut.
strings.d7.s2.name: Blue Elephant Phuket
strings.d7.s2.tips: Royal Thai cuisine in a mansion. A fitting farewell lunch, and cooking classes are available too.
strings.d7.s3.name: Phuket Airport Road Sirinat
strings.d7.s3.tips: The airport is 45 minutes away. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ka Jok See Phuket
strings.d7.b0.tips: Thai food in an old house.
strings.d7.b1.name: Sirinat National Park Nai Yang
strings.d7.b1.tips: A beach next to the airport, where you can watch planes land.
strings.note0: There is no public transport in Phuket. Use a scooter (licence and helmet required), Grab or a hotel taxi. Tuk-tuks are expensive, so haggle.
strings.note1: November to April is dry with calm seas, so Phi Phi and Similan tours run reliably. December and January are the busiest months.
strings.note2: Book boat tours online with hotel pickup included. Bring seasickness tablets and reef-safe sunscreen.
strings.note3: Choose your seafood by the kilo at Rawai market; the cooking fee is charged separately per person.
strings.note4: Cover shoulders and knees at temples. On Bangla Road, ask the drink price first.
strings.note5: Skip elephant rides and choose ethical sanctuaries instead.
